correctness.rationale: For one-dimensional multiplication-closed lines, units are forced to be the unique scalar-unit line and nilpotent radical generators satisfy x^2=0. Exterior grading gives x^2=2a∧b+b∧b; characteristic-two Frobenius kills every radical element. Over odd characteristic, alternating-bivector normal form proves b²=0 iff b has rank at most two, and a∧b=0 iff a is in the supporting two-plane. Gaussian counting and explicit degree-strata partition prove every coefficient over every finite field. The standalone checker independently exhausts full radicals for n=4,q=2 and n=3,q=3, plus degree-one/two pairs n=4,q=3; these experiments are not the proof.

value.rationale: Every local algebra has a natural set of 1D multiplication-closed subspaces, stratified by radical powers. This theorem gives its entire depth polynomial for a canonical infinite family of exterior quotients and reveals a characteristic-two discontinuity and the first degree-four Plücker rank obstruction. It is neither a single arbitrary parameter example nor merely a computational reproduction of an existing table; the exact invariant is a coherent starting point for further subalgebra enumeration.
